question.problem: Estimate the area under the curve $y=-{x}^{2}+3x+1$ over the interval $[1.5,3.5]$ using a left Riemann sum with step size $Δx=0.5.$ Is this an overestimate or an underestimate?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14221930/assets/ad1e85721eb2142f5cad422530aeed86c0919f34261d19e11e9f056cf355b387.png)

The area $A$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{f(1.5)+f(2)+f(2.5)+f(3)}})\cdot {{Δx}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $f(x)$ at each point:

| $x$ | $1.5$ | $2$ | $2.5$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $3.25$ | $3$ | $2.25$ | $1$ |

Finally, we obtain the following approximation for our area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(3.25+3+2.25+1)\cdot 0.5 \\  & =9.5\cdot 0.5 \\  & =4.75\end{aligned}
$$

Because the function is *strictly decreasing* over the interval $[1.5,3.5],$ the rectangles reach *above* the function, which means our approximation is an *overestimate* of the actual area.
